job.domain: a coding assistant working in a repository

items.text:
# transit-alerts

Small service that polls the regional rail operator's disruption feed and posts a daily digest to our team Slack channel. It was written during the spring strike and has been running unattended since.

## How the alert levels work

The feed publishes a `severity` field that maps loosely onto the operator's own wording. We collapse it into three buckets: `info`, `delay` and `cancelled`. Anything the operator marks as an *official strike notice* is always promoted to `cancelled` regardless of the raw value, because in practice the raw value lags behind the announcement by an hour or two. The mapping lives in `src/severity.ts`; if the operator renames a field the tests there will fail loudly rather than silently downgrade a strike to a delay.

## Prompt template for the digest

When we render the Slack message we fill a small template (`templates/digest.hbs`) with the day's summary. The template has a `prompt` line at the top — a short human-readable nudge like "Check before you leave" — followed by the affected lines. Please keep that line under 60 characters; anything longer wraps badly on mobile.

## Notes for contributors

- Do not reply to the feed's webhook with a 4xx on unknown event types; the operator sends new types without warning and a non-2xx makes them retry aggressively, which once flooded us with duplicates.
- The `previous` run's state is stored in Redis under `transit:state:lastday`. Clear it manually if you're testing the catch-up logic.
- Issues tagged `rules` refer to the severity mapping, not to the feed's terms of service. The actual ToS summary is in `docs/operator-tos.md`.

Lease addendum, unit 4B — parking and storage. Tenant is allocated one covered space (P-12) and one storage locker (S-07, basement level). The space is not transferable and may not be sublet separately from the apartment. Bicycles may be kept in the locker but not in the shared stairwell, per the fire rules posted by the entrance. If the landlord reassigns spaces during repaving works, the tenant will be given seven days' written notice of the new assignment. Questions about the lease should go to the managing agent, not the building's front desk.
README badge fix: the `strike` workflow name was renamed to `rail-disruption` last week, so update the link in the header before the next release.

## Apartment handover checklist (draft)

We're finalising the checklist the letting agent will use when we hand the flat back at the end of the tenancy. It should be practical and, above all, match what the lease actually says — last time we lost part of the deposit over a box of old paint tins nobody had written down anywhere.

### What's already covered

Meter readings on the day, keys returned in person, a signed copy of the inventory. The agent's own template covers most of this, but it references the *previous* tenancy agreement in two places (clause numbers no longer match), so we'll maintain our own version in `docs/handover.md` and link the lease PDF.

### Still to add

- Photographs of every room, timestamped.
- A note that the landlord's "professional clean" rule only applies if the lease says so — ours doesn't, and the agent keeps implying otherwise.
- The utilities switch-over form, which the agent is supposed to supply but never does.

### Wording

The tone should be businesslike. Avoid anything that reads like a demand; the agent is slow but cooperative. If a line item is genuinely disputed, note it and move on rather than arguing in the document.

The offsite booking is finally confirmed: Cedar Lodge, Thursday and Friday, with the return coach leaving at 16:00 sharp. Please book travel yourself through the portal rather than replying to the calendar invite, because the organiser is reconciling headcount from the portal export. If the rail strike on Thursday affects your line, there's a fallback coach from the park-and-ride at 07:15 — mention it in the travel channel so we know who's on it. Dietary requirements go to Priya by Tuesday.
The `lease-renewal` cron job should skip February; the agent's office is closed and last year it spammed the shared inbox.

On the strike days the operator is running a reduced timetable, so the 07:52 fast service is cancelled and only the stopping train runs, roughly every 40 minutes. Our usual advice stands: leave earlier than you think you need to and check the live departures board before setting off. The season-ticket refund form is in the shared drive under `finance/travel/refunds`, and it needs a copy of your ticket plus the dates affected. Refunds are processed in batches at the end of the month, so don't expect the money back immediately.

### Lease review meeting — notes

The three of us went through the renewal offer clause by clause. Overall it's fair, but there are two points worth pushing back on before we sign.

**Rent review.** The proposed uplift is above the local average, and the lease ties it to a formula the agent hasn't shown us. We'll ask for the index they used and a worked example for our current figure. If they can't produce it, that's a reasonable basis to negotiate.

**Break clause.** The draft gives us a six-month break with two months' notice. That's tighter than the previous agreement, which allowed three months. We should ask for the previous terms to be reinstated, or at minimum a written explanation for the change.

**Housekeeping.** The deposit scheme certificate is missing from the pack; chase the agent. The inventory references furniture that isn't in the flat, so photograph everything before the new term starts. Finally, the building's fire-safety rules were updated last month — the notice is by the main door and applies from the start of the new term, so read it and note anything that affects the balcony.
`offsite-budget.csv` still has the previous year's figures in the travel column — replace them before the finance review.
